title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: Second line of the U-list: the punctured neighbourhood D*×C* is labelled with Δ_1^* (and a hat) in the manuscript; it should be U^*_{Δ_2^*,X}. This is a slip.

Identifications such as U_{Δ_1^*,X} = C*×D are only valid up to homotopy or locally (as models of tubes). The margin note itself seems to flag the formulas as heuristic. No genuine mathematical error otherwise; the count of 16 is consistent.

ideas.what: Decomposing a normal-crossings stratified space into strata, tubular neighbourhoods and partially/fully punctured tubes (local models products of C, C*, D, D*, pt), to be reglued via canonical maps
ideas.modern_name: Dévissage of stratified spaces via links/tubes; exit-path ∞-category; homotopy links (Quinn); unzipping (Ayala–Francis–Tanaka); Kato–Nakayama / real oriented blow-up local models
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom–Mather (tubes), Quinn (homotopy links, 1988), MacPherson/Treumann/Lurie (exit paths), Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2010s), Kato–Nakayama (1999)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 ('topologie modérée', dévissage of stratified structures, application to the Mumford–Deligne boundary of M_{g,ν}) as a programme only; this explicit local computation is not published

ideas.what: Counting/indexing the elementary 'types' by flags of strata together with choices of which boundary parts are deleted (16 types for the crossing of two divisors)
ideas.modern_name: Strata of a poset-stratified space / cells of the exit-path category; local combinatorics of a normal crossings divisor

ideas.what: Expectation of explicit 'correspondences' between the types making up a stratification (general formalism referenced pp. 74' ff.)
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of link/tube data; constructible-sheaf / stratified homotopy hypothesis

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a programme to describe the homotopy type/topos of a normal-crossings stratified space, ultimately the boundary of M̄_{g,ν}, as a finite diagram of elementary 'types' glued via canonical maps. He anticipates explicit correspondences between types. The general formalism is not completed here and is essentially subsumed today by exit-path and stratified-homotopy theory.
missed.quote: Il me semble donc plausible que ces types, une fois mis en liste, [ont] une correspondance entre eux qu'il faudrait expliciter
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically shows Grothendieck working out the 'dévissage' of Esquisse §5 in concrete local terms. It is mathematically routine relative to modern stratified homotopy theory (Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka) and log-geometric local models.

deep.surprise_reason: A concrete worked example of the stratified dévissage programme announced in Esquisse d'un programme. The content (tubes of the coordinate cross in C^2 and their product models) is elementary and fully covered by later stratified homotopy theory; of archival interest only.
transcription_corrections: Line 1–2: 'une [-...-] fois mis en liste, une correspondance' is probably 'ces types, une fois mis en liste, [ont] des correspondances entre eux'.
Likely 'simplifiant'/'s'explicitant' unclear; 'exprimer tous les types correspondants associés à [une] stratification, analogue[s] pp 74' ff.'
'ilimitables[?]' is more likely 'élémentaires' (interlinear insertion), and 's'opposent' is probably 's'imposent': '4×4 = 16 types élémentaires qui s'imposent d'une certaine façon'.
'ℙ' denotes a point (pt), not a projective line: Δ_1 = C×pt, Δ_2 = pt×C, D_2 = pt.
Second U^* line: manuscript writes U^{(^)}_{Δ_1^*,X} = D*×C*; meaning U^*_{Δ_2^*,X} (author's slip).
Margin note plausibly: 'Les écritures sont bien entendu purement heuristiques – pour les remplacer par des formules correctes, il faudrait … !' (low confidence).
